pr_title: Fix mqtt config validation error handling
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
When an invalid yaml config is found, this no longer fails mqtt starting up. This PR fixes some cases where processing an invalid config, and fails logging a correct  error message.

This PR fixes correct logging an invalid config in case:

- A `ValueError` was raised during config validation, causing not to log the by the caller intended error message.
- A YAML config contains mappings or lists causing the generation of the YAML config in the issue reported contain unwanted diagnostic information. And caused failing generating a hash over the config to be used as issue ID.
- A `config` with an invalid `entity_category` for `sensor` or `binary_sensor` was used in a configuration. These validation issues were caused by #101471

This broke mqtt: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/103414 this extended the config entity check to binary sensors, which have not been fixed upstream in mqtt.
It did not, https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/101471 is effectively the cause. #103414 was just to make sure a proper error message was raised.
#101471 does not check binary_senors domain (to be complete it probably should). But for mqtt a check was added here for binary sensors.
Right, did not realize that. To be consequent we should handle `binary_sensor` in the same way
May be we should just allow the setting for a couple of months and raise an issue?

Similar problem with Aqara presence detector FP1 (RTCZCGQ11LM) by Xiaomi
![изображение](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/95581374/2ced5471-3144-4975-aed8-81ef483c2655)

`config` in an invalid entity category for sensor, as a sensor can not be configured. See documentation. https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/

Changes to enforce validation were added to the sensor base class.

Solution is setting the entity category to `diagnostic` or leaving the config setting away.

https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/29651

May be this change (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/101471) should have been a breaking change.
Thanks, I removed the sensors manually.
I will open a PR to ensure the error handling is correct. That PR will close this issue when it is merged.

With the correct warning (in 2023.11), the behavior is effectively breaking some integrations (some custom integrations at least, see https://github.com/kamaradclimber/heishamon-homeassistant/issues/163).

I think it would have deserved a breaking change mention because setting an entity as config was a legitimate understanding of the documentation (I understand doc has been updated to be clearer :+1: )
Am sorry this was not added to the patch release. But a fix will be added to HA Core 2023.12
